Sign restrictions combined with zero restrictions (Arias, Rubio-Ramirez & Waggoner 2018)

Source: R/id-extra.R
id_zerosign.Rd

Let \(\Theta_h = \Phi_h L Q\) be the structural IRF at horizon \(h\), with \(LL'=\Sigma\) and \(Q\) orthogonal, and \(\Theta_\infty = (I-\sum_l A_l)^{-1} L Q\). A zero restriction on the response of variable \(i\) to shock \(j\) at horizon \(h\) reads \(e_i'\Phi_h L\, q_j = 0\), linear in the column \(q_j\). Following ARRW Algorithm 2, shocks are processed in decreasing order of their number of zero restrictions \(z_j\); column \(q_j\) is drawn uniformly on the unit sphere of the null space of \([Z_j L;\ q_1';\dots;q_{j-1}']\), which exists iff \(z_{(j)} \le K-j\). The draw is kept if all sign restrictions (up to a per-shock sign flip) hold. Zeros hold exactly by construction and \(PP'=\Sigma\).

Usage

id_zerosign(
  sign = NULL,
  zero = NULL,
  zero_lr = NULL,
  horizon = 1L,
  zero_horizon = 1L,
  nrot = 1L,
  maxtry = 1000L
)

Arguments

sign

K x K matrix or K x K x H array of +1/-1/0 as in id_sign() (NULL for none).

zero

K x K matrix or K x K x H array with 1 where the response (variable x shock) is zero at that horizon (impact only when a matrix: zero_horizon = 1).

zero_lr

K x K 0/1 matrix, 1 = long-run (cumulative) response is zero.

horizon

horizon count over which a matrix sign is imposed.

zero_horizon

horizon count for a matrix zero (default 1: impact only).

nrot, maxtry

as in id_sign().

Value

a varm_id object (usable in irf() on varm_draws/varm).

Details

Missing importance weights. ARRW additionally reweight draws by a Jacobian term (\(|\det A_0|^{-(2n+m+1)}\) over \(\prod_i |\det V_i|\)) so that they are uniform on the restricted set under the conjugate prior. These weights are NOT implemented here: accepted draws are unweighted samples from the null-space sampler, which is the exact ARRW posterior only when no zero restrictions are present (then it coincides with id_sign()) or when the zero restrictions fully pin down the rotation up to sign (then the weights are constant across rotations, though they still vary over the reduced-form draws). Treat bands under partial zero-restriction identification as approximate.

Economic intuition. Use it when theory gives a few exact zeros (e.g. monetary policy has no contemporaneous effect on output and prices, or a demand shock has no long-run effect on output) and signs for the rest. Pitfalls: bands mix identification uncertainty and sampling uncertainty; the implied prior over impulse responses is informative; zeros on many shocks can make the problem exactly identified (sign information then irrelevant).

See also

id_sign(), id_restrictions(), irf_fry_pagan()

Other identification: id_hetero(), id_proxy(), id_restrictions(), identification, irf_fry_pagan(), proxy_draws()

Examples

S <- matrix(0, 3, 3)
S[1, 1] <- 1
S[3, 3] <- 1
Z <- matrix(0, 3, 3)
Z[3, 2] <- 1
id <- id_zerosign(S, Z)
irf(draws(varm(yraw, p = 2), "mc", 20), id, horizon = 4)
#> <varm IRF> K = 3, horizon 0..4, id = zerosign, bands: 68%/90%
#> sign-restriction acceptance rate: 1
